newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares extend gains ahead of H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares extend gains ahead of H1 results.

text.p: Estonian shares extended recent gains in lighter trade ahead of first half results which are expected to be good, dealers said.
Unlike the market in neighbouring Latvia, which has languished after a four-day weekend, Estonia's market has charged out of the holiday with a full head of steam.
Total trade was 63.7 million kroons compared to 110.7 million kroons on Wednesday and the Talse index gained 1.69 percent to 277.93.
Dealers said the market is expecting good first half results and 1997 profit revisions and falls are not seen.
"First half audited results may give an important impression to western investors...who take into account audited results instead of monthly balance sheets," one dealer said.
Hoiupank rose five kroons to 151 kroons in trade of 10.3 million kroons as the market responded to news that Sweden's Swedbank was set to up its stake in the bank.
Swedbank said on Thursday that it had reached an agreement with the Estonian central bank to acquire 7.4 percent of the bank's shares, which would raise its stake to 19.9 percent.
On the free market, privatisation vouchers were most traded in trade of 2.2 million kroons.
